P2.critique: The strongest analytic cross-check in the batch, and the only one that is genuinely independent of the CAD kernel. For an involute gear there is no textbook closed form, so the agent wrote a separate polar integration of the exact involute boundary (unwind angle offset via inv(alpha) = tan(alpha) - alpha, bisection onto the flank, 400k samples, summing 0.5*rho^2 dtheta over one tooth pitch and multiplying by z) in plain python with no FreeCAD import. Result: 'independent profile area: 272.5308700775457 / independent volume: 83067.40919963593' versus the OCC model's 272.5307032239148 / 83067.06210244277 -- rel. diff 4.2e-6, attributed correctly to BSpline interpolation of the flank versus the exact curve. This was computed BEFORE finishing and is the evidence on which the agent based its P5 decision.

P4.critique: num_turns=16, 14 Bash + 1 Write, 143 s, $0.640 -- roughly double the two clean trials on every axis. Batching was decent where it mattered (spec write + spec_consistency + '=== GATE ===' + geometry in one call), and there was no GUI or interactive wait. But the detour budget is exceeded: (1) pip/PYTHONPATH fumbling cost 4 turns (pip --user, pip --user --ignore-installed, ls -ld + sys.path inspection, then `PYTHONPATH= pip install --user`); (2) scorer-API rediscovery cost a further 5 turns, two of them outright errors -- `AttributeError: 'HeuristicSpecConsistencyScorer' object has no attribute 'compare'`, then dir() to find `.score`, then ConsistencyChecker signature probing, then `AttributeError: 'ConsistencyReport' object has no attribute 'findings'`, then finally `rep.model_dump()`. That is 9 of 16 turns spent rediscovering plumbing that has nothing to do with the part. Judged fail on the '~3 detours' bar; the mitigating fact is that the second cluster was purposeful diagnosis of a real 0.4286 score rather than aimless flailing, which is why confidence is 0.62 rather than high.

P5.critique: This is the criterion's live test case and the agent passed it deliberately, not accidentally. spec_consistency reported 3 inconsistent + 1 not_found, and every one of the four is a DERIVED gear quantity the generic heuristic mis-measured: gear_module (1.5875) not_found; pressure_angle measured 16.7079 deg off 'GearProfile.LineAngle[0,4]' against spec 20; diametral_pitch 'measured' as 304.8 off 'plane_pair_0.offset' (it grabbed the pad length -- a nonsense match for a 1/inch quantity); pitch_diameter measured 22.2177 off 'circular_pattern_0.pattern_radius x 2' against spec 19.05. The agent obtained that per-parameter breakdown, recognised the mis-measurement, and explicitly declined to touch the geometry: 'I did not distort geometry that already matches its analytic volume to chase them.' It had the independent 400k-sample involute integration (rel. diff 4.2e-6) as the positive evidence that the geometry was right, so the refusal is grounded, not stubborn. The correct behaviour: it treated a low heuristic score as a measurement artefact, having first PROVEN the geometry independently. One deviation to record: the agent chose outer_diameter = 22.225 (standard m*(z+2)) over the spec's printed 22.352 and said so openly -- that is a design-time convention call made before any finding, not phantom-chasing, and it argued it from gear standards rather than from the scorer.

notes: The gear is the batch's most informative trajectory. It is the ONE case where the spec-consistency heuristic breaks down badly (0.4286 on geometry that is provably correct to 4.2e-6), and the agent handled it exactly right: prove the geometry independently, then refuse to deform it for the scorer. Two structural facts fall out. (1) The scorer's derived-parameter matches are not merely absent, they are actively wrong -- diametral_pitch was matched to the 304.8 mm pad length, pitch_diameter to a pattern radius. Any downstream use of spec_consistency as a reward signal on gear-family parts would reward exactly the distortion P5 forbids. (2) The 9-of-16 turns burned on pip and scorer-API rediscovery is pure per-task overhead that will recur identically on every one of 100 tasks.
